record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let f(x₁, x₂, …, x_n) be a complex polynomial such that all moments ∫₀¹⋯∫₀¹ f(x₁, …, x_n)^m dx₁⋯dx_n vanish for every m ≥ 1. Determine whether this forces f to be the zero polynomial.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Let f(x1,x 2,...,xn) be a polynomial in C[x1,x 2,···,xn] such that the following moment conditions hold Mm := ∫1 0 ∫1 0 ··· ∫1 0 fm(x1,x 2,...,xn) dx1 dx2···dxn = 0, m ≥1. Is it true that f = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and let $f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with complex coefficients. Suppose that all moments of the powers of $f$ over the unit cube vanish, i.e.
$$M_m \;:=\; \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \cdots \int_0^1 f(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)^m \, dx_1\, dx_2 \cdots dx_n \;=\; 0 \quad \text{for every integer } m \geq 1.$$
Determine whether these conditions force $f \equiv 0$. Equivalently, decide whether there exists a nonzero polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ such that $\int_{[0,1]^n} f^m = 0$ for all $m \geq 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classical polynomial moment problem (univariate, with general endpoints and a weight) has been extensively studied and solved by Pakovich and Muzychuk in terms of composition decompositions, but the specific multivariate formulation over the unit cube—asking whether vanishing of all integer-power integrals of a complex polynomial in n variables forces it to be identically zero—does not appear to have a published resolution. It is listed as an open problem in low-dimensional dynamics surveys, and no source found verifies a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Solution of the polynomial moment problem
status_evidence.snippet: Pakovich–Muzychuk solve the (univariate) polynomial moment problem in terms of composition decompositions of polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The univariate polynomial moment problem has been solved, but in a different (composition-theoretic) formulation; the multivariate cube version is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Fedor Pakovich – publications
status_evidence.snippet: Lists works on polynomial and Laurent polynomial moment problems, all in one variable.
status_evidence.claim: Available literature on the polynomial moment problem concerns the one-variable case; the multivariate version remains unresolved in this list.
